A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same soft-label topic-modeling research, despite the DSL-Topic renaming. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original topic-quality, retrieval, ablation and sensitivity results on 20NewsGroup, TweetTopic and StackOverflow.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations of further model variants, hidden-state layers and target sparsity.

M1.justification: The stated reconstruction objective changes from KL(prediction || target) in v1 to KL(target || prediction) in v2. V2 also extends the framework from ProdLDA to ECRTM and FASTopic while preserving their respective regularizers. These are substantive formulation and backbone adaptations; the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate topic modeling and label-based document retrieval on the same three datasets, with identical dataset statistics in Table 5. Additional model configurations and sensitivity experiments remain within this coverage; multimodal modeling is only proposed as future work.

E2.justification: The corresponding main and qualitative comparisons retain LDA, ProdLDA, CombinedTM, ZeroshotTM, ETM, BERTopic, ECRTM and FASTopic. Additional language models and DSL backbones are variants of the proposed approach, rather than additions to the external baseline set.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands from one backbone with three language models to three backbones with five, adding Qwen3.5-0.8B and Phi-3-mini. New experiments vary hidden-state layers and target truncation. Table 4 changes from K=50 examples using a randomly selected seed to K=75 cases selected for the largest coherence margins. The main metrics and topic-count grid remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds layer-selection experiments in Appendix H and target-sparsity experiments in Appendix I, testing input representation and coherence–diversity control. Table 4 replaces the earlier qualitative examples and adds per-word leave-one-out coherence analysis. The original component ablations, prompt sensitivity, temperature analysis and vocabulary-size analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Five seeds per topic count, Welch tests and prompt-sensitivity ANOVA are retained; the new statement of 20 measurements per cell merely makes existing aggregation explicit. However, v1 Table 7 displays significance highlights that are absent from corresponding v2 Table 10, despite its caption still promising them. This is a limited loss of statistical reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive backbone/teacher results and new diagnostic results, and replaces qualitative topic lists. Retained values also change: Table 2 ERNIE StackOverflow P@5 changes from .588 to .754, while Table 1 Llama-1B 20NewsGroup Purity changes from .559 to .564. All 44 original per-topic-count rows and Table 3 ablation values remain unchanged. The revised objective prevents treating the retrieval changes as established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix I develops a reverse-KL projection argument specialized to ProdLDA. V2 Section 3.4 and Appendix J introduce a broader structured model family and latent-concept posterior-predictive interpretation, replace the projection direction, and derive forward-KL equivalence to dense cross-entropy. V2 also makes the main objective's regularization sign consistent with the appendix.

C1.justification: The principal claims about semantic reconstruction, improved topic quality and assignment, and useful retrieval representations are retained. V2 modestly broadens the contribution framing into a general DSL distillation framework with a Bayesian characterization. Retrieval becomes a separately enumerated contribution, but was already claimed in v1's abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: V2 adds an implicit-to-explicit Bayesian interpretation and explains backbone-dependent trade-offs through a proposed mismatch between dense targets and FASTopic's transport solver. It recommends ProdLDA as the practical default and discusses FASTopic's retrieval failures. The impact statement additionally addresses biases inherited through LM distillation and limitations of using coherent topics in sensitive applications.

D1.justification: V2 supplies an implementation repository address, replacing v1's release promise and supplementary-code reference. It newly specifies single-token vocabulary filtering, retrieval KL direction and query exclusion, and integration settings for the added backbones. These improve documentation without establishing that the previously unspecified procedures changed; repository availability was not independently checked.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands the conceptual positioning through knowledge distillation and implicit Bayesian inference, citing Hinton et al., Xie et al., Wang et al. and Li et al. It also adds references for the new teachers and layer analysis while removing several earlier background citations. The existing topic-model related-work taxonomy largely remains.

P1.justification: Beyond the DSL-Topic title and terminology, v2 extensively rewrites the introduction, objective exposition, mathematical appendix and baseline documentation. It reorganizes metric explanations, moves the complete-results appendix from E to K, replaces the impact statement, adds acknowledgments and removes the AI-assistance paragraph. These constitute substantial editorial restructuring.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is replaced with a document-level example and Figure 2 is redrawn. Tables 1–2 gain backbone groupings, Table 4 introduces coherence scores and word-contribution coloring, and two diagnostic tables are added. The detailed results become four subtables across two pages. Figures 3–5 retain their plotted content despite relocation and resizing.

improvement.justification: V2 provides useful evidence that the approach extends beyond ProdLDA, adds targeted design checks, and improves reproducibility documentation and consistency between the main objective and appendix. These gains outweigh limited reporting losses. However, unexplained revisions to retained retrieval scores, selection of favorable qualitative cases, and missing appendix significance highlights limit confidence in a larger overall improvement.
